supremacy-definition: Section I, p.1: the paper states 'Quantum supremacy is achieved when ...' as its own working definition, in context of its own proposal.
task-sampling-random-circuits: Abstract, p.1 and Section I, p.1: the paper states the task it studies. 'Natural task' is attributed to the authors in the value.
cross-entropy-difference-definition: Section II.B, p.4: Eq. (10) defines the cross entropy difference as H0 minus H(pA,pU); the paper names it there.
assumption-classical-output-uncorrelated: Section II.A, p.4: 'we assume that the output of a classical algorithm with polynomial cost is almost statistically uncorrelated with pU(x)'. It is an assumption of the paper's own analysis, stated as such.
assumption-sufficient-depth: Section II.A, p.4, before Eq. (7): 'we assume that we use random circuits of sufficient depth such that ...'. A stated condition of its own derivation.
supremacy-criterion-alpha-above-C: Section II.B, p.5, Eqs. (12)-(13): the paper states its own operational criterion, 1 >= alpha > C, with C bounded by the best known classical algorithm executed on an existing computer.
experimental-sample-size-m: Section II.B, p.5, step 2 of the paper's proposed estimation procedure: 'm ~ 10^3 - 10^6'. A parameter of its own proposed protocol.
alpha-cannot-be-measured-directly-at-sca: Section II.B, p.5: the paper states that for large circuits pU(x_exp) cannot be computed, so alpha cannot be measured directly. A limit on its own method, stated by the authors.
practical-limits-on-alpha-threshold: Section II.B, p.5: the paper lists three practical limits on the alpha needed to claim supremacy (lower bound on C, number of measurements, experimental biases). Limits on its own proposal.
depolarizing-error-simulation-setup: Section III, p.6: the paper states how errors are emulated in its simulations: 15 two-Pauli products at r2/15 after each two-qubit gate, a random single Pauli at r1/3 after each one-qubit gate.
circuit-family-optimized-for-convergence: Section IV, p.7: 'The following circuits were chosen through numerical optimizations to minimize the convergence time to Porter-Thomas.' The paper's own circuit design choice.
circuit-construction: Section IV, p.7, steps 1, 2(a), 2(b): the paper's own circuit construction (Hadamard cycle, CZ in eight configurations, random single-qubit gates from {X1/2, Y1/2, T} on qubits not in a CZ).
single-qubit-gate-placement-rules: Section IV, p.7: the three placement rules are stated as part of the paper's own circuit construction.
x-half-y-half-gate-definition: Section IV, p.7: the paper defines X1/2 (Y1/2) as a pi/2 rotation about the X (Y) axis of the Bloch sphere.
no-final-hadamard-layer-in-simulation: Section IV, p.7: 'We did not apply a final cycle of Hadamards in the numerical study because it would double the computational run time.' A statement of its own simulation protocol. The type should be setup, not measured.
hardness-argument-scope-iqp-extension: Section V, p.9: 'In this section we will extend the method ... (IQP) [23, 29] to the general case of universal random circuits.' States what the section covers; whether the argument succeeds is not claimed by this item.
appendix-b-simulator-optimizations: Appendix B, p.14: 'We perform a number of single- and multi-node optimizations, including vectorization, multi-threading, cache blocking, as well as gate specialization'; Section B 2 (pp.14-15) describes each.
appendix-b-edison-hardware: Appendix B 3, p.15: the paper states the machine its simulations ran on (Cray XC30 at NERSC, #39 in TOP500, 5,576 compute nodes).
appendix-c-treewidth-quickbb: Appendix C, p.17: 'The upper bounds were obtained by running the QuickBB algorithm [91].' States how the paper's own Figure 13 bounds were computed.
appendix-h-bayesian-path-sampling-algori: Appendix H, p.20: the paper defines the algorithm it analyzes there ('The approximation algorithm considered here is a Bayesian estimation ...').

theory_low.footnote-l1-distance-2-over-e: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Footnote 3, p.3 gives the 2/e value and the 'few measurements suffice' remark with no derivation.
theory_low.cross-entropy-difference-unity-and-zero: Section II.B, p.4: stated with a pointer to Eqs. (3) and (8). Those equations rest on Porter-Thomas and 'sufficient depth' assumptions with approximate equality (Eq. 7), and are an informal derivation, not a labelled theorem with a proof. Not a proved result.
theory_low.fidelity-approx-cross-entropy-difference: Section III, p.6, Eq. (18): obtained 'under this ansatz', the authors' numerical observation that pU(x) and the error-state probabilities are almost uncorrelated (Fig. 3, App. A). Approximate, not a proved result.
theory_low.gumbel-for-uniform-sampling: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section III, p.7, after Eq. (21): one sentence, no derivation.
theory_low.hardness-argument-conditional-on-conject: Section V.A, p.10: a heuristic argument that rests on a conjecture ('If we conjecture that a sufficient large fraction ... is as hard ... as the worst case') and on the proof in Ref. [29]. Not a proved result.
theory_low.output-prob-maps-to-quasi-3d-ising: Section V.A, p.10: a forward claim ('We will show in the next section'). The mapping is built in V.B, but 'no apparent structure that makes it easier to approximate' is the authors' interpretation, not a proved statement. Graded by the weaker.
theory_low.amplitude-as-feynman-path-integral: textbook, stated not proved (F129). Section V.B, p.10: Eq. (24) is a sum over intermediate basis states; the sentence only says it 'can be viewed as' a Feynman path integral.
theory_low.amplitude-is-ising-partition-function: Section V.B, pp.10-11: the construction (Eqs. 26-37) is shown, but the text says 'one can see from comparing', omits H^(2)(x) ('we do not provide its explicit form') and drops constant phases. It is an informal derivation, not a stated and proved theorem.
theory_low.ising-coupling-distribution-decays-expon: Section V.B, p.12, Eqs. (38)-(39): derived under stated simplifying assumptions (random CZ layout, equal gate probabilities, pCZ about 1/4, approximate ratios). An approximate derivation, not a proved result.
theory_low.coupling-graph-quasi-three-dimensional: Section V.B, p.12: a summary description ('In summary ... represents a quasi three-dimensional structure') that rests on the approximate ensemble analysis of Eqs. (38)-(43). Interpretation, not a proved result.
theory_low.appendix-b-expected-communication-slowdo: Appendix B 3, p.15: the bandwidth values are cited to [89]; the 8x slowdown is a performance-model estimate ('we expect'), not a measurement or a proved result.
theory_low.appendix-g-reviews-sampling-implies-np-o: Appendix G, p.19: 'we review' and 'We follow the proof from Ref. [29]'. The argument is a cited proof (Bremner, Montanaro, Shepherd) adapted, and it relies on the Stockmeyer Counting Theorem, which App. F only outlines. Not a proved result in this paper.
theory_low.appendix-g-multiplicative-error-quarter: Appendix G, p.19, after Eq. (G6): depends on the Porter-Thomas assumption taken from the paper's own numerics and on the proof of Ref. [29]; the epsilon symbols are lost in the text layer. Not a proved result in this paper.
theory_low.appendix-h-equivalent-fidelity-q2-over-N: Appendix H, pp.20-22, Eq. (H24): obtained by a long calculation with approximations (Q much less than L, first-order Taylor terms kept, rho_bar taken at its expectation). Written as 'alpha ~ Q^2/NL', an approximate scaling, not a labelled theorem with a full proof.
theory_low.appendix-h-fidelity-1e-52-for-1e18-paths: Appendix H, p.20: a numerical instance of the approximate scaling alpha ~ Q^2/(NL), with L ~ 2^250 for 7x6 qubits and depth 25 stated without derivation. Depends on the low-graded approximation.
